# discord_invite (Resource)

Manages a Discord channel invite. Invites are immutable, so any change recreates the invite.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "discord_invite" "welcome" {
  channel_id = "123456789012345678"
  max_age    = 86400 # 24 hours
  max_uses   = 0     # unlimited
  temporary  = false
}

output "invite_url" {
  value = discord_invite.welcome.url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the channel the invite targets. Changing this forces a new invite.

### Optional

- `max_age` (Number) Duration in seconds before expiry (0 = never). Default 86400 (24h). Changing forces a new invite.
- `max_uses` (Number) Maximum number of uses (0 = unlimited). Changing forces a new invite.
- `temporary` (Boolean) Whether the invite grants temporary membership. Changing forces a new invite.
- `unique` (Boolean) Whether to always create a new unique invite rather than reuse a similar one. Changing forces a new invite.

### Read-Only

- `code` (String) The unique invite code (also the resource ID).
- `guild_id` (String) Snowflake ID of the guild the invite belongs to.
- `url` (String) The full invite URL (https://discord.gg/<code>).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Invites are imported using their code. Create-time settings (max_age, etc.)
# cannot be recovered and reflect schema defaults after import.
terraform import discord_invite.welcome abcd1234
```
